headline: Nation-state phishing, an extortion arrest and AI governance
standfirst: A China-nexus group targeting AI policy experts leads the day, alongside an alleged ShinyHunters arrest, a new federal AI task force, and widening AI data-access questions at Google and Anthropic. No CVEs appear in today's selection.
bodyMarkdown:
## Research

TA419, described as a China-nexus espionage group, is running credential phishing against AI experts at U.S. think tanks, universities and legal-sector organizations [[s4]]. The campaigns impersonated prominent economists, AI policymakers and a prominent Anthropic employee, singling out an AI policy expert. The excerpt truncates there, so the targeting rationale beyond impersonation is not established.

Analysis: given its rank and the nation-state attribution, this is the story to read for the AI policy ecosystem's exposure — though the excerpt does not detail the phishing infrastructure or whether any access succeeded.

## Industry

A suspected ShinyHunters member using the alias "Rey," named as Saif al-Din Khader, has reportedly been detained in Jordan and is said to be cooperating with the FBI, according to people familiar with the matter [[s3]]. If confirmed, it could disrupt an active extortion group and yield intelligence on other members — a conditional the excerpt supports as reporting, not established fact.

Separately, Jay Clayton, the National Intelligence Director, has been named to lead a new federal AI task force, after a White House meeting with AI executives [[s1]]. The excerpt does not describe the task force's mandate or authorities. Analysis: pairing intelligence leadership with AI policy implies a governance shift, but the excerpt supports only the appointment.

On the product side, Gemini could gain broad access to files, apps and the web on macOS, with actions taken without per-action permission prompts [[s5]]; Anthropic is asking Claude users to voluntarily share voice conversations for model training [[s2]]. Both are permission-and-consent questions rather than disclosed vulnerabilities.
